## Notes (not failing lines)

* **N-1 (K42).** No test passes a band set whose ids differ from the six default bands. A mutant that reads the
  granularity rows for the default ids instead of `set.bands` therefore survives. The promise is C-0155's "the optional
  `set` is any `{ bands, cuts }`", which C-0166 (1) inherits. No M0 path can produce such a set. `bands.json` ships the
  six, and a town's `FieldBands` carries the band set's ids, which only an M1 table edit (§7.6) could rename. The
  checker's mirror probe (a two-band set `low` / `high`, depth 10–20 / 20–40, read at the cut 0.5 → 15–30) passes on
  the item's code and kills K42. One such assertion in `granularityBands.test.ts` would close the gap in a later round
  of this folder's owner. PLAUSIBLE that it matters before M1.
* **N-2 (K10).** The `Number.isFinite(ctxValue)` guard is redundant with the range comparisons. It is kept as
  documentation; no test is needed.
* **N-3 (gates).** The whole-tree lint and build were red for a few minutes on M0-a-11's in-flight
  `kernel/src/skeleton/engine.ts` (`globalThis` / `console` debug lines), not on this item. Both were re-run green
  after that seat removed them (step 3). The item's own files linted clean throughout.
* **N-4 (shipped expectations).** `shipped.test.ts` derives its expectations from the shipped rows through the same
  `bandInterpolate`, so that the AFTER-M-1 re-fit never edits it (C-0166 (4)). By design, it cannot detect a wrong
  number inside a shipped table. The design's numbers are held by the fixture tests here and by M0-s-02's pins
  (`golden.json`'s version-1 pin of granularity.json and regimes.json; `ladder.test.ts`'s 1.1 / 1 / 0.9 / 0.95). The
  checker's probe confirmed that the shipped tables give the design's rows today.
